classification.difficultyReason: Compare two flights using exact trigonometric components and demonstrate equal ranges.

content.prompt: A stone is thrown at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $60^\circ$. At the same time and place, a second stone is thrown at the same speed but at $30^\circ$. Use $g=10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

spec.description: Two projectile paths with common launch and landing points, initial velocity arrows, speed labels and angles measured from the positive horizontal. Ordinary marks use black; trajectories use standard blue.
spec.mathematics: For horizontal coordinate x, the paths are y=sqrt(3)x-x²/20 and y=x/sqrt(3)-x²/60, both ending at x=20sqrt(3).
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied question diagram; no calculated values are labelled.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Which stone finishes its flight first and by how long? Give the time difference exactly and to 1 d.p.

answer.short: The stone thrown at $30^\circ$ lands first, by $2\sqrt3-2\text{ s}\approx1.5\text{ s}$.
answer.worked:
For the stone thrown at $60^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned}x_1&=10t\\y_1&=10\sqrt3t-5t^2\end{aligned}$$
For the stone thrown at $30^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned}x_2&=10\sqrt3t\\y_2&=10t-5t^2\end{aligned}$$
Set each vertical displacement to zero and take the positive time.
$$\begin{aligned}0&=t(10\sqrt3-5t)\\t_1&=2\sqrt3\text{ s}\\0&=t(10-5t)\\t_2&=2\text{ s}\\t_1-t_2&=2\sqrt3-2\text{ s}\\&\approx1.5\text{ s}\end{aligned}$$
The stone thrown at $30^\circ$ lands first.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that the 2 stones land at the same place.

answer.short: Both land $20\sqrt3\text{ m}$ from the common launch point.
answer.worked:
Substitute each positive landing time into its horizontal displacement equation.
$$\begin{aligned}x_1(2\sqrt3)&=10(2\sqrt3)\\&=20\sqrt3\text{ m}\\x_2(2)&=10\sqrt3(2)\\&=20\sqrt3\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
Both stones start at the same point and travel in the same horizontal direction, so they land at the same place.
